questions.q: What does every Salesforce sandbox copy from production, regardless of type?
options: Metadata only -- objects, fields, page layouts, Flows, Apex, permission sets -- as of creation or last refresh
All of production's real records, with no exceptions
Nothing at all until a sandbox template is applied
Only the Account and Contact objects
questions.explain: Every sandbox type copies metadata; whether it also copies real records depends on which of the four sandbox types you choose.

questions.q: Which sandbox type is designed to copy a sampled subset of production records, controlled by a saved sandbox template?
options: Developer
Developer Pro
Partial Copy
Full
questions.explain: Partial Copy sandboxes use a sandbox template -- a saved definition of which objects and how many records of each to include -- to copy a realistic but limited sample, up to 5 GB.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say defaulting to a Full sandbox "to be safe" is usually the wrong choice?
options: Because Full sandboxes cannot run Flows or Apex
Because a Full sandbox is the slowest to refresh, most expensive to maintain, and carries the most privacy exposure, when a smaller type would have met the actual need
Because Full sandboxes are only available to Salesforce employees
Because Full sandboxes do not include any metadata at all
questions.explain: An architect should match sandbox type to actual purpose -- reaching for Full by default when a Partial Copy or Developer sandbox would do means paying unnecessary storage, refresh-time, and data-exposure costs.

questions.q: What is a notable licensing constraint on Full sandboxes that this lesson calls out as a planning input?
options: Only Developer sandboxes require any additional license
Full sandboxes can only be created once per calendar year regardless of edition
Full sandboxes are included free with every Salesforce edition with no exceptions
Full sandboxes typically come with Unlimited and Performance editions, or must be purchased separately in editions that don't include them
questions.explain: An architect designing environment strategy for an org on a lower edition may need to explicitly budget for a Full sandbox license, or design the testing approach around not having one.

questions.q: In the default mapping of sandbox types onto the promotion path from Lesson 1, which sandbox type is typically used for the Development tier?
options: Full, because development needs the most realistic data available
Partial Copy, because development needs a sampled subset of production records
Developer or Developer Pro, because development is metadata-only work that doesn't require real records
No sandbox type is used for development -- it happens directly in production
questions.explain: Development is fast, cheap, iterative building that doesn't need real data, which is exactly what the metadata-only Developer and Developer Pro sandboxes are built for.
